review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

18:1.sourceText: Ταῦτα εἰπὼν Ἰησοῦς ἐξῆλθεν σὺν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ πέραν τοῦ χειμάρρου τῶν Κέδρων, ὅπου ἦν κῆπος, εἰς ὃν εἰσῆλθεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.
18:1.targetText: After Jesus had spoken these words, He went out with His disciples across the Kidron Valley, where they entered a garden.

groups.note: The participle εἰπών supplies the After-clause.
χείμαρρος ("winter torrent, ravine") is rendered Valley.
Κέδρων here is the place name Kidron.
αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ("He and His disciples") is rendered they.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB's Greek text has a different word at this point in the name phrase, and no English word renders this article.
BSB compresses "where there was a garden, into which they entered" to "where they entered a garden", so ἦν ("there was") and the relative ὅν ("which") have no English word.
The preposition repeats the verb's prefix and is absorbed in English entered.

18:2.sourceText: ᾔδει δὲ καὶ Ἰούδας ὁ παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν τὸν τόπον, ὅτι πολλάκις συνήχθη Ἰησοῦς ἐκεῖ μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ.
18:2.targetText: Now Judas His betrayer also knew the place, because Jesus had often met there with His disciples.

groups.note: The article with the participle παραδιδούς ("the one betraying") is rendered betrayer.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

18:3.targetText: So Judas brought a band of soldiers and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees. They arrived at the garden carrying lanterns, torches, and weapons.

groups.note: ἐκεῖ ("there") is rendered at the garden.
μετά ("with") is rendered carrying.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not repeat from the before Pharisees, so the second ἐκ and its article have no English word.
The καί between the first two items is represented by a comma in BSB's list.

18:4.targetText: Jesus, knowing all that was coming upon Him, stepped forward and asked them, “Whom are you seeking?”

groups.note: The article with the participle ἐρχόμενα ("the things coming") is rendered that was coming.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves οὖν untranslated.

The article with the participle παραδιδούς ("the one betraying") is rendered betrayer.

18:10.sourceText: Σίμων οὖν Πέτρος ἔχων μάχαιραν εἵλκυσεν αὐτὴν καὶ ἔπαισεν τὸν τοῦ ἀρχιερέως δοῦλον καὶ ἀπέκοψεν αὐτοῦ τὸ ὠτάριον τὸ δεξιόν. ἦν δὲ ὄνομα τῷ δούλῳ Μάλχος.
18:10.targetText: Then Simon Peter drew his sword and struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his right ear. The servant’s name was Malchus.

groups.note: Greek having a sword ... drew it is compressed as drew his sword. The possession participle, actual sword noun and anaphoric it refer to the one sword and jointly supply the English possession phrase; having alone does not mean his.
Greek dative to/for the servant in the naming statement is expressed by the English possessive The servants; this actual case-marked noun phrase carries the ownership relation.

18:37.targetText: “Then You are a king!” Pilate said.  “You say that I am a king,” Jesus answered. “For this reason I was born and have come into the world, to testify to the truth. Everyone who belongs to the truth listens to My voice.”
